course_description:
Lectures and seminars illustrating how brain systems work in an integrated fashion to extract high level sensory information, plan and control movement, form memories, cope with emotional and physical stress, and adapt to drugs of addiction.

This course is composed of several major themes that focus on how systems in the brain work together to extract high-level sensory information, plan and control movement, lay down memories, and the central mechanisms that give rise to and cope with cognition, emotion,ﾠtrauma, andﾠdisease. The course builds on previous cellular and systems physiology and neuroscience knowledge to develop a high-level conception of how systems of neurons work together to respond to changes in the organism, from animals to humans. In addition to lectures on these themes, students will learn in detail about a particular brain system by critically analysing and presenting primary scientific literature in a group seminar setting.

course_aims:
This course is composed of ten major themes that focus on how systems in the brain work together to extract high level sensory information, to plan and control movement or lay down memories, and the central mechanisms that give rise to and cope with, stress, emotion, mood, injury, homeostasis and addiction.

This integrated approach is designed to address some of the areas not previously covered in the undergraduate curriculum, to allow for individual active learning in an area of the student's choice and to leave the student with the view that an individual is more than the sum of their channels, circuits and systems.

learning_outcomes.description: Draw together the neuroscience streams encountered by the student in previous undergraduate disciplines.
Provide an integrated view of how neural systems interact to achieve a goal directed outcome.
Make an in-depth analysis of the published scientific literature.
Make an oral and visual presentation of scientific results using appropriate information and communication techniques.
Justify a scientific position based on literature research and scientific knowledge.
Know the major regions of the central nervous system - gross neuroanatomy.

Describe the principles of brain connectivity, including axonal development, pathfinding, large scale study of the whole brain connectome in animals and humans, and neurological conditions that arise from defects in connectivity.
Describe how the nervous system processes somatosensory inputs. Know about how the internal representation of the outside world is built on a ‘neural code’.

Describe the neural circuits that transform intention into action. Understand how cortical and subcortical networks coordinate movement, with emphasis on basal ganglia and their roles in action selection, motor learning, and neurological disorders.
Describe how the brain processes visual inputs.

Describe the key features of the epileptic state, what can cause epilepsy and how the brain adapts to this state; describe the brain circuits involved in epilepsy, and how knowledge of epilepsy-induced changes in brain state can guide treatment for epilepsy. Including metabolic treatment options.
Describe the neurobiology of psychosis in humans and animal models.
Describe the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the brain regions involved in giving rise to consciousness and our sense of self.
Describe the cognitive changes with age. How exercise increases neurogenesis, improves cognitive function to improve well-being.

Describe how the brain responds to injury at a cellular and molecular level, develop a broad understanding of the hurdles and challenges that need to be overcome for brain repair and provide a critical and informed judgement on the value and importance of findings from experimental research around neurotrauma and repair.

assessment_details.title: Journal Club Oral Presentation
assessment_details.task_description: Each student will be assigned to a Journal Club, which will meet regularly. In these clubs, students will be asked to give an oral presentation on a topic paper to the remainder of the group. All students presenting will be marked by your Journal Club Leader - criteria marking sheets used for marking will be supplied. The date of your presentation will be determined by negotiation with the Journal Club Leader. Oral Presentation 18%: All oral presentation marks will be moderated by the NEUR3002 course coordinator, to ensure equitable marking across all Journal Clubs. You will receive your Journal Club mark after the moderation process, and prior to the end of semester examination. Active participation is required in Journal Club discussions. To assess participation, students will complete a feedback form for the topic paper discussed in each Journal Club session (unless they are presenting in that session). All students should be prepared to contribute to the discussion of other students' presentations. This participation will be noted by the Journal Club Leader. This is a pass/fail assessment. Students are expected to attend all Journal Club sessions. Students who miss a club must inform their Journal Club Leader. If they miss two or more club meetings, the Journal Club Leader will inform the course coordinator. If a student missing more than two clubs - they will receive zero marks for their participation sub-section. Students who are at risk of missing three or more sessions, please contact your Journal Club Leader to discuss available options. You must complete a feedback sheet prior to each Journal Club Presentation and submit it to your Journal Club Leader via email. Further details of the assessment format and marking criteria will be provided on Blackboard during the semester. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct . As this assessment is not recorded re-marks are not permitted as per the Assessment Procedure (Clause 114). Please note post marking moderation will occur. The Connected Brain 1 [Stefan Thor] How the brain regulates connections. Basic principles of neuronal connectivity. Axon/dendrite pathfinding, and methods for studying axon/dendrite projections. Molecular genetic pathways underlying axon/dendrite pathfinding. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07
The Connected Brain 2 [Stefan Thor] How the brain regulates connections.Large-scale efforts aimed at resolving the mouse and human connectome. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07
The Connected Brain 3 [Stefan Thor] How the brain regulates connections. How defects in connectivity may underlie a number of human neurological disorders. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07

The Sensing Brain 1 [Rodrigo Suarez] The Sensing Brain 1: Somatotopy and modularity in functional neural systems. Sensory transduction and peripheral coding in touch perception. Receptive fields and cross-modal processing. Ascending pathways for fine versus crude touch.

The Sensing Brain 2: [Rodrigo Suarez] The Sensing Brain 2: Functional neuroanatomy of touch pathways. Central processing, cortical neuron coding and synaptic plasticity in touch. Referred pain and phantom limb phenomena.

The Sensing Brain 3: The Sensing Brain 3: Comparative neuroanatomy of sensory pathways. Evolution and development of sensory specialisations in vertebrates follows lifestyle. Pre-sensory spontaneous neural activity shapes sensory pathways. Critical periods and early sensory experience refine sensory systems.

The Moving Brain 1 [Dehorter] The “Moving Brain" lecture series will explore the neural circuits that transform intention into action. Students will examine how cortical and subcortical networks coordinate movement, with a particular focus on the basal ganglia and their roles in action selection, motor learning, and neurological disorders. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L09

The Moving Brain 2 [Dehorter] The “Moving Brain" lecture series will explore the neural circuits that transform intention into action. Students will examine how cortical and subcortical networks coordinate movement, with a particular focus on the basal ganglia and their roles in action selection, motor learning, and neurological disorders. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L09

The Moving Brain 3 [Dehorter] The “Moving Brain" lecture series will explore the neural circuits that transform intention into action. Students will examine how cortical and subcortical networks coordinate movement, with a particular focus on the basal ganglia and their roles in action selection, motor learning, and neurological disorders. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L09
The Seeing Brain 1 [Ulrike Siebeck] Humans are visual creatures. These lectures will cover how vision occurs from the retina to cortical processing. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L10
The Seeing Brain 2 [Ulrike Siebeck] Humans are visual creatures. These lectures will cover how vision occurs from the retina to cortical processing. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L10
The Seeing Brain 3 [Ulrike Siebeck] Humans are visual creatures. These lectures will cover how vision occurs from the retina to cortical processing. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L10

The Epileptic Brain 1 [Karin Borges] These lectures on epilepsy will discuss the pathophysiology of this group of diseases with seizures and current treatments. We will then learn about strategies for treatment development for treatment-resistant people with epilepsy and metabolic treatment options. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L11

The Epileptic Brain 2 [Karin Borges] These lectures on epilepsy will discuss the pathophysiology of this group of diseases with seizures and current treatments. We will then learn about strategies for treatment development for treatment-resistant people with epilepsy and metabolic treatment options. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L11

The Epileptic Brain 3 [Karin Borges] These lectures on epilepsy will discuss the pathophysiology of this group of diseases with seizures and current treatments. We will then learn about strategies for treatment development for treatment-resistant people with epilepsy and metabolic treatment options. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L11
Revision tutorial [Thor to Borges] This Tutorial will cover key aspects from lectures given by Drs Thor, Suarez, Dehorter, Siebeck and Borges in preparation for the Mid Semester Exam

The Psychotic Brain 1 [Thomas Burne] This lecture series explores the neurobiology of psychotic disorders in humans and preclinical animal models, with a particular focus on schizophrenia. The first lecture provides an overview of the diagnosis, epidemiology, and neurobiological basis of psychosis. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L12

The Psychotic Brain 2 [Thomas Burne] The second lecture examines the genetic and environmental risk factors associated with schizophrenia and introduces the animal models used to investigate its underlying mechanisms. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L12

The Psychotic Brain 3 [Thomas Burne] The third lecture focuses on the cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia, including impairments in attention and executive function, which are core features of the disorder. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L12

The Conscious Brain 1 [Van Swinderen] Altered states and what they tell us about consciousness. General anaesthesia: mechanisms and theories. Sleep: Evolutionary considerations and the functions of different sleep stages. Wakeful states: Selective attention, illusions, psychedelics, disorders of consciousness. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L13

The Conscious Brain 2 [Van Swinderen] Theories of consciousness. Brief historical perspective, a deluge of different theories. The way forward with 'consciousness probes', e.g., Perturbational Complexity Index, and global oddballs. Current debates surrounding Global Workspace, IIT, predictive processing, etc. Meat machines debate; how much biology is required? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L13
